chunks: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the words of God, Mighty and Majestic: 'Whoever slays a soul, unless it be for manslaughter... it is as though he slew all the people' [5:32].
He said: 'For him is a seat in the Fire. Even if he had killed all the people altogether, he would not be returned except to that very seat.'

key_terms.النَّار: The Fire — a Quranic term for Hell (Jahannam), the place of punishment in the afterlife
key_terms.مَقْعَد: A seat or place — here denoting a reserved place in Hell assigned to the murderer
key_terms.نَفْس: Soul or person — in Islamic law, 'killing a soul without right' refers to unlawful homicide (qatl al-'amd)

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Baqir say about the punishment of murder in the Quran (5:32)?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) interprets the Quranic verse about the gravity of murder (5:32) to mean that the murderer has a fixed seat reserved in Hell. The Imam emphasizes that this punishment is fixed and absolute — even if the killer were to multiply his crimes and kill everyone, he would still return to that same seat. This ruling underscores the irreversible spiritual consequence of unlawful killing in Islamic law.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, altogether from Hammad Bin Isa, from Rabie Bin Abdullah, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said, ‘I asked Abu Ja’farasws about the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [5:32] whoever slays a soul, unless it be for manslaughter . . . it is as though he slew all the people.
He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘For him is a seat in the Fire, had he killed the people altogether, he would not have been Returned, except to that (very) place’.
